source_text: Ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸ ἐκ τῶν ἐπιγείων κάτωθεν ἄρξασθαι καὶ λέγειν τὴν ποίησιν τῶν γεγενημένων ἀνθρώπινον καὶ ταπεινὸν καὶ πάνυ ἀσθενὲς τὸ ἐννόημα αὐτοῦ, ὡς πρὸς θεόν, ἐστίν. Ἄνθρωπος γὰρ κάτω ὢν ἄρχεται ἐκ τῆς γῆς οἰκοδομεῖν, καὶ οὐ πρὸς τάξιν δύναται καὶ τὴν ὀροφὴν ποιῆσαι ἐὰν μὴ τὸν θεμέλιον ὑπόθηται. Θεοῦ δὲ τὸ δυνατὸν ἐν τούτῳ δείκνυται ἵνα πρῶτον μὲν ἐξ οὐκ ὄντων ποιῇ τὰ γινόμενα, καὶ ὡς βούλεται. Τὰ γὰρ παρὰ ἀνθρώποις ἀδύνατα δυνατά ἐστιν παρὰ θεῷ. Διὸ καὶ ὁ προφήτης πρῶτον εἴρηκεν τὴν ποίησιν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ γεγενῆσθαι τρόπον ἐπέχοντα ὀροφῆς, λέγων· Ἐν ἀρχῇ ἐποίησεν ὁ θεὸς τὸν οὐρανόν, τουτέστιν διὰ τῆς ἀρχῆς γεγενῆσθαι τὸν οὐρανόν, καθὼς ἔφθημεν δεδηλωκέναι. Γῆν δὲ λέγει δυνάμει ἔδαφος καὶ θεμέλιον, ἄβυσσον δὲ τὴν πληθὺν τῶν ὑδάτων, καὶ σκότος διὰ τὸ τὸν οὐρανὸν γεγονότα ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ ἐσκεπακέναι καθαπερεὶ πῶμα τὰ ὕδατα σὺν τῇ γῇ, πνεῦμα δὲ τὸ ἐπιφερόμενον ἐπάνω τοῦ ὕδατος ὃ ἔδωκεν ὁ θεὸς εἰς ζωογόνησιν τῇ κτίσει, καθάπερ ἀνθρώπῳ ψυχήν, τῷ λεπτῷ τὸ λεπτὸν συγκεράσας (τὸ γὰρ πνεῦμα λεπτὸν καὶ τὸ ὕδωρ λεπτόν), ὅπως τὸ μὲν πνεῦμα τρέφῃ τὸ ὕδωρ, τὸ δὲ ὕδωρ σὺν τῷ πνεύματι τρέφῃ τὴν κτίσιν διϊκνούμενον πανταχόσε. Ἕν μὲν τὸ πνεῦμα φωτὸς τύπον ἐπέχον ἐμεσίτευεν τοῦ ὕδατος καὶ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, ἵνα τρόπῳ τινὶ μὴ κοινωνῇ τὸ σκότος τῷ οὐρανῷ ἐγγυτέρῳ ὄντι τοῦ θεοῦ, πρὸ τοῦ εἰπεῖν τὸν θεόν· Γενηθήτω φῶς. Ὥσπερ οὖν καμάρα ὁ οὐρανὸς ὢν συνεῖχε τὴν ὕλην βώλῳ ἐοικυῖαν. Καὶ γὰρ εἴρηκεν περὶ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἕτερος προφήτης ὀνόματι Ἠσαΐας, λέγων· Θεὸς οὗτος ὁ ποιήσας τὸν οὐρανὸν ὡς καμάραν καὶ διατείνας ὡς σκηνὴν κατοικεῖσθαι. Ἡ διάταξις οὖν τοῦ θεοῦ, τοῦτό ἐστιν ὁ λόγος αὐτοῦ, φαίνων ὥσπερ λύχνος ἐν οἰκήματι συνεχομένῳ, ἐφώτισεν τὴν ὑπ᾿ οὐρανόν, χωρὶς μὲν τοῦ κόσμου ποιήσας. Καὶ τὸ μὲν φῶς ὁ θεὸς ἐκάλεσεν ἡμέραν, τὸ δὲ σκότος νύκτα· ἐπεί τοί γε ἄνθρωπος οὐκ ἂν ᾔδει καλεῖν τὸ φῶς ἡμέραν ἢ τὸ σκότος νύκτα, ἀλλ᾿ οὐδὲ μὲν τὰ λοιπά, εἰ μὴ τὴν ὀνομασίαν εἰλήφει ἀπὸ τοῦ ποιήσαντος αὐτὰ θεοῦ.Τῇ μὲν οὖν πρώτῃ ὑποθέσει τῆς ἱστορίας, καὶ γενέσεως τοῦ κόσμου, εἴρηκεν ἡ ἁγία γραφὴ οὐ περὶ τούτου τοῦ στερεωματος, ἀλλὰ περὶ ἑτέρου οὐρανοῦ τοῦ ἀοράτου ἡμῖν ὄντος, μεθ᾿ ὅν οὗτος ὁ ὁρατὸς ἡμῖν οὐρανὸς κέκληται στερέωμα, ἐφ᾿ ᾧ ἀνείληπται τὸ ἥμισυ τοῦ ὕδατος, ὅπως ᾖ τῇ ἀνθρωπότητι εἰς ὑετοὺς καὶ ὄμβρους καὶ δρόσους. Τὸ δὲ ἥμισυ ὕδατος ὑπελείφθη ἐν τῇ γῇ εἰς ποταμοὺς καὶ πηγὰς καὶ θαλάσσας. Ἔτι οὖν συνέχοντος τοῦ ὕδατος τὴν γῆν, μάλιστα κοίλους τόπους, ἐποίησεν ὁ θεὸς διὰ τοῦ λόγου αὐτοῦ τὸ ὕδωρ συναχθῆναι εἰς συναγωγὴν μίαν, καὶ ὁρατὴν γενηθῆναι τὴν ξηράν, πρότερον γεγονυῖαν αὐτὴν ἀόρατον.Ὁρατὴ οὖν ἡ γῆ γενομένη ἔτι ὑπῆρχεν ἀκατασκεύαστος. Κατεσκεύασεν οὖν αὐτὴν καὶ κατεκόσμησεν ὁ θεὸς διὰ παντοδαπῶν χλοῶν καὶ σπερμάτων καὶ φυτῶν.
pass_a_gloss: But also the one beginning from the things on earth below to speak and to say the making of the things that have come to be is human and lowly and very weak the thought of him, as towards God, it is. For a human being being below begins to build from the earth, and not towards order is he able and to make the roof if not the foundation he lays down. But of God the powerful is shown in this, that first he makes the things that come to be from not being, and as he wishes. For the things impossible with humans are possible with God. Wherefore also the prophet first spoke the making of the heaven to have come to be in a manner holding a roof, saying: In the beginning God made the heaven, that is through the beginning the heaven came to be, as we have shown to have been declared. And earth he says is powerful ground and foundation, and abyss is the multitude of the waters, and darkness because God covered the heaven which came to be, like a lid, the waters with the earth, and spirit is the one being brought upon the water which God gave for quickening the creation, just as to a human soul, to the fine the fine mixing (for the spirit is fine and the water is fine), so that the spirit may nourish the water, and the water with the spirit may nourish the creation passing through everywhere. One is the spirit holding a type of light mediating between the water and the heaven, so that in some way the darkness may not share with the heaven being near to God, before God said: Let light come to be. Just as, therefore, the heaven being a vault held the matter like a lump. And another prophet, named Isaiah, also spoke about the heaven, saying: God is the one who made the heaven like a vault and stretched it out like a tent to dwell. The arrangement of God, that is his Word, shining like a lamp in a contained house, illuminated the area under the heaven, having made it without the world. And God called the light day, and the darkness night; for indeed a human would not have known to call the light day or the darkness night, but not even the rest, if he had not received the naming from God who made them. In the first hypothesis of the story and genesis of the world, the holy scripture spoke not about this solid but about another heaven, the invisible one to us, after which this visible heaven to us is called solid, upon which half of the water is taken up, so that it may be for humanity for rains and showers and dews. And the other half of the water was left on the earth for rivers and springs and seas. Still, therefore, the water holding the earth, especially the hollow places, God made the water through his Word to be gathered into one gathering, and the dry land to become visible, which previously had become invisible. The earth, therefore, having become visible, still existed unprepared. God, therefore, prepared it and adorned it with all kinds of grasses and seeds and plants.

pass_b_english: But to start from earthly things below and call the making of created things human, lowly, and very weak in its conception toward God — that is what it is. A human, being low, begins building from the ground, yet cannot achieve order and make a roof unless he first lays a foundation. God's power, however, is shown in this: he first makes what comes to be from non‑being, and does so as he wishes. What is impossible for humans is possible for God. Therefore the prophet first spoke of the heaven's making as holding the character of a roof, saying, 'In the beginning God made the heaven' — that is, through the beginning the heaven came to be, as we have already shown (Genesis 1:1). He calls earth powerful ground and foundation; abyss is the mass of the waters; darkness exists because the heaven God made covered the waters and the earth like a lid. Spirit is what was brought upon the water, which God gave to quicken creation, just as a soul to a human — the fine mingling with the fine (for spirit is fine and water is fine) — so that the spirit may nourish the water, and the water together with the spirit may nourish creation, passing through everywhere. The one spirit, bearing a likeness of light, mediated between the water and the heaven, so that in some way darkness might not share with the heaven, which is nearer to God, before God said, 'Let light come to be.' Just as the heaven, being a vault, held the matter like a lump. And another prophet, named Isaiah, also spoke of the heaven, saying, 'God is the one who made the heaven like a vault and stretched it out like a tent to dwell' (Isaiah 40:22). God's arrangement — that is, his Word — shining like a lamp in an enclosed room, illuminated the region under heaven, having made it apart from the world. God called the light day and the darkness night; for a human would not have known to call the light day or the darkness night, nor anything else, had he not received the naming from the God who made them.

In the first premise of the history and genesis of the world, holy Scripture spoke not of this firmament but of another heaven, invisible to us, after which this visible heaven is called firmament — the one upon which half the water was taken up, so that it might serve humanity for rains, showers, and dews. The other half of the water was left on the earth for rivers, springs, and seas. While the water still held the earth, especially the hollow places, God through his Word made the water gather into one gathering and the dry land become visible, though it had previously been invisible. The earth, now visible, still existed unprepared. God therefore prepared and adorned it with all kinds of grasses, seeds, and plants.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text. Pass A provides a literal gloss, while Pass B provides a fluent translation. Both correctly handle the complex theological distinctions regarding the 'invisible heaven' and the 'firmament'. Scripture citations (Genesis 1:1 and Isaiah 40:22) are correctly added to Pass B to identify the quoted/alluded prophetic passages as required by the instructions.
